S27.01.needs: A signed-in account that can generate documents in Chat
S27.01.note: The card and viewer use the document's title, and the default comes from the artifact title helpers (artifactTitle.ts, artifactDisplayTitle falls back to artifactKindTitle), which I did not confirm end to end; the old quoted lines in the plan are gone, so this is from the current files, and I could not confirm the exact default text a person would see for an untitled document.
steps: Sign in and open Chat.
Send a message that asks for a written document, for example a short one-page plan.
Wait for the answer to show a document card, and read the title shown on the card.
Tap the card to open the document full screen.
Compare the title at the top of the full-screen view with the title on the card, and check that it is not blank.
S27.01.where: Chat (first screen after signing in) > ask for a document > tap the document card in the answer > read the title at the top of the full-screen view, shown as the title followed by " · Document"

S27.29.needs: A document with at least two versions (ask for a change once, or edit it, before starting)
S27.29.note: The version counter is a button with an accessibility label rather than a visible word, and the times depend on formatVersionTime in apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/versionSummary.ts, which I did not run.
steps: Open a document that has been changed at least once, for example by asking for changes in Chat, so it has more than one version.
In the document's top bar, tap the version counter (it shows the version number out of the total).
Read the "Version history" sheet: check that each past version is listed with its time.
Tap an older version row to view it, then check that the document shows that version's content.
Tap "Restore" on that older row, then check that the document content returns to that version and that a newer entry is kept in the history.
S27.29.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the version counter in the top bar (accessibility hint "Opens the version history") > "Version history" sheet > tap a version row to view it, or tap "Restore" on an older row

S27.35.needs: A signed-in account with a document open; a Mac app that opens .docx files
S27.35.note: The Word option appears for document-type artifacts that are not slide decks (artifactExport.ts lines 88-96); the sheet only opens when there is more than one export choice, so a single-choice file would download directly.
steps: Open a document in Chat so the full-screen view shows.
Tap the download icon in the top bar. It has no visible words; VoiceOver reads it as "Download artifact".
In the sheet headed "Download as", look for the option "Word" with the detail "A .docx document you can edit".
Tap "Word" and wait for the share or save step to appear.
Open the saved or shared file on the Mac and check that it is a Word document with the document's text.
S27.35.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the download icon in the top bar (accessibility label "Download artifact") > "Download as" sheet > tap "Word"

S27.36.needs: A signed-in account with a document open
S27.36.note: The PDF option appears for document-type artifacts (artifactExport.ts lines 88-95) and the export itself runs through apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/artifactExport.ts exportArtifact; I did not run it.
steps: Open a document in Chat so the full-screen view shows.
Tap the download icon in the top bar. It has no visible words; VoiceOver reads it as "Download artifact".
In the sheet headed "Download as", look for the option "PDF" with the detail "A styled document".
Tap "PDF" and wait for the share or save step to appear.

S27.36.where: Chat > open a document (tap its card) > tap the download icon in the top bar (accessibility label "Download artifact") > "Download as" sheet > tap "PDF"
